additions.reason: The spring (מַעְיָן) is explicitly identified as the שֵׂכֶל (intellect) via bechina language. It belongs in Package 1 alongside שֵׂכֶל and חָכְמָה.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל לְחַדֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה, אֲזַי מַתְחִיל לִנְבֹּעַ מַעְיָן, בִּבְחִינַת: וּמַעְיָן מִבֵּית ה' יֵצֵא, שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׂכֶל

additions.reason: The intellect (שֵׂכֶל) is the central good concept of Package 1. The spring is identified as the sekhel. It is the divine intellectual vitality that begins to flow when Torah is innovated.
additions.source_quote: מַעְיָן מִבֵּית ה' יֵצֵא, שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׂכֶל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בְּחָכְמָה יִבָּנֶה בָּיִת

additions.reason: Wisdom (חָכְמָה) is equated to the spring/sekhel via the proof-verse 'בְּחָכְמָה יִבָּנֶה בָּיִת' (Proverbs 24). The Rebbe uses this verse to show that the spring is the sekhel and that sekhel = chokhmah. Wisdom is a bechina of the spring of intellect.
additions.source_quote: מַעְיָן מִבֵּית ה' יֵצֵא, שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׂכֶל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בְּחָכְמָה יִבָּנֶה בָּיִת

additions.reason: Weeping (בְּכִי) is the dominant concept of Package 2. It is explicitly identified via bechina language in two separate verses: once in 'מִבְּכִי נְהָרוֹת חִבֵּשׁ' (Job 28:11 per Rashi) and once in 'וְשִׁקֻּוַי בִּבְכִי מָסָכְתִּי' (Ps. 102:10). Weeping is the essential nature shared by the masekhta and Talmud Bavli.
additions.source_quote: עַל־יְדֵי הַבְּכִי מְתַקֵּן נְהָרוֹת... וְשִׁקֻּוַי בִּבְכִי מָסָכְתִּי

additions.reason: A tractate (מַסֶּכֶת) is explicitly called a bechina of 'וְשִׁקֻּוַי בִּבְכִי מָסָכְתִּי' — the compilation of halakhot and chiddushim IS the pouring of drink with weeping. This is a direct bechina identification in the text.
additions.source_quote: חִבּוּר הַהֲלָכוֹת וְהַחִדּוּשִׁין נִקְרָא מַסֶּכֶת, זֶה בְּחִינַת: וְשִׁקֻּוַי בִּבְכִי מָסָכְתִּי

additions.reason: The Babylonian Talmud is explicitly called a bechina of 'עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל שָׁם יָשַׁבְנוּ גַּם בָּכִינוּ' (Ps. 137:1). The Rebbe states: 'זֶה בְּחִינַת תַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי'. The 'גַּם בָּכִינוּ' is further identified as a bechina of 'וְשִׁקֻּוַי בִּבְכִי מָסָכְתִּי', linking Talmud Bavli to the entire weeping-tractate cluster.
additions.source_quote: עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל, שָׁם יָשַׁבְנוּ גַּם בָּכִינוּ – זֶה בְּחִינַת תַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי

additions.reason: Rivers are the structural conduit of this Torah — they are sought by both the holy learners and the klipot. The neutral rivers are produced by Torah innovation (eitza), fixed by weeping (eitza), and the entire Torah is about managing access to them.
additions.source_quote: עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה מִמֶּנּוּ נְהָרוֹת, וְהַכֹּל בָּאִים לִשְׁתּוֹת מֵאֵלּוּ הַנְּהָרוֹת

additions.reason: The klipot are the evil force that seeks to drink from the rivers of Torah. They are the evil mirror of the good learners who come to drink. The Rebbe's whole concern about weeping first is precisely to protect against the klipot.
additions.source_quote: יָבוֹאוּ גַּם כֵּן קְלִפּוֹת וְסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לִשְׁתּוֹת גַּם כֵּן מִשָּׁם

additions.reason: The sitra achra appears together with the klipot as the compound evil force of this Torah. Both are bechina of each other in this context — they form the evil domain that parasitizes Torah innovation.
additions.source_quote: קְלִפּוֹת וְסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא... לִשְׁתּוֹת גַּם כֵּן מִשָּׁם

concepts_in_source_not_assigned_to_packa.reason: Torah innovation/chiddush is the eitza-cause that produces the spring. It is NOT a bechina of the spring/sekhel — it produces them. Therefore it does not belong in Package 1 (which is the spring/sekhel identity cluster). It is an independent eitza node. Suggested: leave as an eitza node connecting into Package 1, not as a package member. If the dataset is enriched, it would appear as the source end of an eitza edge pointing to מַעְיָן/שֵׂכֶל.

Academies (yeshivot) are mentioned as where the rivers of Talmud Bavli form: 'שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה אֵצֶל הַיְשִׁיבוֹת'. No explicit bechina language is used, but they are functionally equivalent to the Talmud Bavli formation process. If an edge were to be added, it would likely be eitza (the yeshivot are the location/context that produces the rivers), not bechina. Do not add to Package 2 without explicit bechina language.

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: Package 1 (שֵׂכֶל/מַעְיָן — spring of intellect) mirrors Package 4 (קְלִפּוֹת/סִטְרָא אָחֳרָא — the evil that seeks to drink from that intellect). Package 2 (בְּכִי/מַסֶּכֶת — weeping that protects the rivers) is the antidote to the evil mirror: the weeping satisfies the klipot with their portion before the new rivers of Torah are created.
